To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
base station sleep modes, by reducing power in periods of low load, can significantly improve the energy efficiency in cellular access networks.

i) base station sleep modes are an effective means for improving the energy efficiency of access networks; ii) the energy saving is strongly dependent on the traffic pattern; iii) most of the energy savings can be achieved with just one sleep mode per day; and, iv) for heterogeneous networks, micro-cells should be switched off according to an order that is increasing in load.
